[#hash-digests-compare]
.What each of "Digests" is
[cols="2,1,3,2,1,2",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Output | Security | Standard | Status | In the browser (WebCrypto)

| <<hash-legacy,`md5_128`>>
| 128 bits
| broken: collisions are found in seconds
| RFC 1321
| broken
| no

| <<hash-legacy,`sha1_160`>>
| 160 bits
| broken: chosen-prefix collisions are practical
| RFC 3174, FIPS 180-4
| broken
| SHA-1

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_224`>>
| 224 bits
| 112-bit collision resistance
| FIPS 180-4
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_256`>>
| 256 bits
| 128-bit collision resistance
| FIPS 180-4
| recommended
| SHA-256

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_384`>>
| 384 bits
| 192-bit collision resistance
| FIPS 180-4
| recommended
| SHA-384

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_512`>>
| 512 bits
| 256-bit collision resistance
| FIPS 180-4
| recommended
| SHA-512

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_512_224`>>
| 224 bits
| 112-bit collision resistance
| FIPS 180-4
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_512_256`>>
| 256 bits
| 128-bit collision resistance
| FIPS 180-4
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-sha3,`sha3_224`>>
| 224 bits
| 112-bit collision resistance
| FIPS 202
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-sha3,`sha3_256`>>
| 256 bits
| 128-bit collision resistance
| FIPS 202
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-sha3,`sha3_384`>>
| 384 bits
| 192-bit collision resistance
| FIPS 202
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-sha3,`sha3_512`>>
| 512 bits
| 256-bit collision resistance
| FIPS 202
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-sha3,`shake_128`>>
| any length
| up to 128 bits, and half the output length for collisions
| FIPS 202
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-sha3,`shake_256`>>
| any length
| up to 256 bits, and half the output length for collisions
| FIPS 202
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-keccak,`keccak_256`>>
| 256 bits
| 128-bit collision resistance
| Keccak (the SHA-3 submission's padding), as Ethereum uses it
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-blake2,`blake2b_512`>>
| 512 bits
| 256-bit collision resistance
| RFC 7693
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-blake2,`blake2s_256`>>
| 256 bits
| 128-bit collision resistance
| RFC 7693
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-blake3,`blake3`>>
| 256 bits, or any length
| 128-bit security in every mode
| the BLAKE3 specification (hash, keyed hash, derive_key, extendable output)
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-legacy,`ripemd_128`>>
| 128 bits
| 64-bit collision resistance: too short today
| RIPEMD-128 (Dobbertin, Bosselaers, Preneel)
| legacy
| no

| <<hash-legacy,`ripemd_160`>>
| 160 bits
| 80-bit collision resistance
| RIPEMD-160 (Dobbertin, Bosselaers, Preneel)
| legacy
| no
|===

[#hash-digests-choose]
.How to choose among "Digests"
[cols="2,2,2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Fastest natively | Smallest on Emscripten | Where it is used | Choose it when

| <<hash-legacy,`md5_128`>>
| 919 MiB/s (hash2)
| 8,039 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6151[legacy checksums and old protocols; RFC 6151 retires it for signatures]
| Only to read or check data that already uses it.

| <<hash-legacy,`sha1_160`>>
| 1,197 MiB/s (hash2)
| 10,285 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://git-scm.com/docs/hash-function-transition[Git's original object ids, with collision detection]; link:https://shattered.io/[the first public collision, SHAttered (2017)]; link:https://sha-mbles.github.io/[the first public chosen-prefix collision, SHA-1 is a Shambles (2020)]
| Only to read or check data that already uses it.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_224`>>
| 596 MiB/s (hash2)
| 14,116 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4[FIPS 180-4's shorter SHA-2]
| When a standard asks for it; otherwise SHA-256.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_256`>>
| 592 MiB/s (hash2)
| 14,108 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf[Bitcoin's block and transaction ids (twice)]; link:https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/01.md[Nostr's event ids (NIP-01)]; link:https://git-scm.com/docs/hash-function-transition[Git's SHA-256 object format]; link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#appendix-B.4[TLS 1.3's cipher suites]
| The default digest: interoperable everywhere, in every browser, fast with hardware support.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_384`>>
| 912 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,579 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#appendix-B.4[TLS 1.3's AES-256 cipher suite]
| When a standard asks for 192-bit strength, or a digest that resists length extension within SHA-2.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_512`>>
| 911 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,582 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032#section-5.1[Ed25519's signatures]; link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0039.mediawiki[BIP39's seeds, through PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512]
| When a standard asks for it, or for a 512-bit digest.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_512_224`>>
| 917 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,645 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4[FIPS 180-4's truncated SHA-512]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_512_256`>>
| 913 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,597 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4[FIPS 180-4's truncated SHA-512]
| A 256-bit SHA-2 digest that resists length extension, fast on 64-bit machines.

| <<hash-sha3,`sha3_224`>>
| 731 MiB/s (hash2)
| 7,175 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.202[FIPS 202]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-sha3,`sha3_256`>>
| 691 MiB/s (hash2)
| 7,172 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.203[ML-KEM, NIST's post-quantum key encapsulation]
| A standard 256-bit digest that is not SHA-2, immune to length extension.

| <<hash-sha3,`sha3_384`>>
| 531 MiB/s (hash2)
| 7,140 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.202[FIPS 202]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-sha3,`sha3_512`>>
| 367 MiB/s (hash2)
| 7,142 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.203[ML-KEM, NIST's post-quantum key encapsulation]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-sha3,`shake_128`>>
| 846 MiB/s (hash2)
| 7,151 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.203[ML-KEM's and ML-DSA's matrix expansion]
| To draw a long stream of bytes from one input, at 128-bit security.

| <<hash-sha3,`shake_256`>>
| 687 MiB/s (hash2)
| 7,151 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032#section-5.2[Ed448's signatures]
| To draw a long stream of bytes from one input, at 256-bit security.

| <<hash-keccak,`keccak_256`>>
| 996 MiB/s (xkcp)
| 24,057 bytes (xkcp)
| link:https://ethereum.github.io/yellowpaper/paper.pdf[Ethereum's addresses, transaction ids and state]; link:https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-55[EIP-55's checksummed addresses]
| For Ethereum and every format that names Keccak-256; never in place of SHA3-256.

| <<hash-blake2,`blake2b_512`>>
| 1,616 MiB/s (hash2)
| 11,982 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9106#section-3.2[Argon2's internal hash]; link:https://doc.libsodium.org/hashing/generic_hashing[libsodium's generic hash]
| A fast software digest or keyed hash where SHA-2 has no hardware support.

| <<hash-blake2,`blake2s_256`>>
| 923 MiB/s (hash2)
| 10,974 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.wireguard.com/protocol/[WireGuard's hash, MAC and HKDF]
| For WireGuard-style protocols and 32-bit targets.

| <<hash-blake3,`blake3`>>
| 2,410 MiB/s (blake3)
| 21,252 bytes (blake3)
| link:https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3-specs/blob/master/blake3.pdf[the BLAKE3 specification: a Merkle tree, for verified streaming and content addressing]
| Large data verified in parts, content addressing, and key derivation from a context string.

| <<hash-legacy,`ripemd_128`>>
| 992 MiB/s (hash2)
| 9,421 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://homes.esat.kuleuven.be/~bosselae/ripemd160.html[the RIPEMD family's page]
| Only to read existing data.

| <<hash-legacy,`ripemd_160`>>
| 640 MiB/s (hash2)
| 11,607 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0141.mediawiki[Bitcoin's hash160 (P2PKH, P2WPKH)]
| For Bitcoin's hash160; never in a new design.
|===

The measured columns are doc/measurements.json's (2026-11-16, Apple M5 Max): the native throughput over 1 MiB, or the time of one derivation over `hmac_sha2_256`, of the fastest backend, and the smallest Emscripten program that calls the function; <<hash-measurements>> has every backend on every target. The data was measured on a loaded, shared machine, so close figures may swap at the next measurement.
